clue.text: Historical tax for one joining union in 1707

definitions.meaning: a ... was an old municipal levy, the one you escaped if you got off ...-free
the 1707 Acts of Union joined Scotland to England, so a native of Scotland joined the union then

explanation.surface: A history quiz question about some levy imposed when the parliaments merged in 1707.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: an old local levy, and a person from Scotland, whose nation entered the 1707 union.

clue.text: Call number set up, like a momentous step taken in 1969?

definitions.text: like a momentous step taken in 1969?

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them

explanation.surface: Phoning someone about Armstrong's moon landing, the famous step of 1969.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns NAMENO round. Armstrong's 'one small step for man' was taken by a single person, so the step was a one-man affair.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1969 moon step was taken by one person alone, so it was a solo, single-person act; the question mark flags the playful reading.

clue.text: France's extremely dated monarch, unwelcome visitor

parts.note: très is the French word for very or extremely
passé means out of date
R, for Rex or Regina, is the abbreviation for a monarch

explanation.surface: A French king who is hopelessly old-fashioned and not wanted around.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who enters land without permission is, by definition, a visitor nobody invited.

clue.text: Prepares for 2027 and 2029, for example

definitions.meaning: to prime something is to make it ready, as with a pump or a wall before painting
each of these two years is divisible only by itself and one

explanation.surface: Getting ready for a couple of upcoming years.
explanation.definitionFit: Priming is preparing; and 2027 and 2029 are both whole numbers with no divisors except one and themselves.

clue.text: 16th-century music distracted capital over half a century

indicators.note: in a down clue the capital sits over, that is above, the next piece

parts.note: someone driven distracted is mad with worry
Riga is the capital of Latvia
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, half of a hundred

explanation.surface: Renaissance music that sent a capital city crazy for fifty years.
explanation.definitionFit: The madrigal, a part-song for unaccompanied voices, flourished in the 1500s in Italy and England.

clue.text: Article penned by second-century bishop, one undermining union

indicators.note: something penned by others is enclosed by them, so the article goes inside the three letters

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grammatical article written by an early church bishop, who undermined a union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One undermining union' is a trade-union sense: the worker who crosses a picket line.
explanation.definitionFit: A strikebreaker is called a blackleg or scab, someone who weakens a trade union by working during a strike.

clue.text: Military exercises that started to link two countries in 1988

definitions.text: that started to link two countries in 1988
definitions.meaning: boring of the Channel Tunnel between Britain and France began in 1988

explanation.surface: Army manoeuvres that began a link between two nations in the late eighties.
explanation.definitionFit: Training routines for troops are drills, and the Channel Tunnel was created by boring through rock from 1988.

clue.text: Parts of every year produce confusion, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak says the word that means produce confusion is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to daze someone is to stun or confuse them

explanation.surface: Bits of the calendar that leave you bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is made up of 365 or 366 twenty-four-hour units, so these are its parts.

clue.text: Plant, during historical period, run inside spy organisation

indicators.note: inside says these pieces go within the letters of the spy agency

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency
in means during, as in 'in winter'
an era is a period of history
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A mole planted inside an intelligence service at some point in history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' tempts as a spy planted in the agency; it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Cineraria is a daisy-family flower, often grown as a pot plant for its bright blooms.

clue.text: See 20
Source of news heard in 1045 and 1115, for instance

definitions.meaning: spoken aloud as ten forty-five and eleven fifteen, these figures are clock readings, not years

explanation.surface: A newspaper that was being heard about in the eleventh and twelfth centuries.
explanation.walkthrough: In a puzzle full of years, 1045 and 1115 look like dates; read as on a 24-hour clock they are hours and minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Times is a British national newspaper, and 10:45 and 11:15 are examples of clock readings.

clue.text: See 26
They're out every year, you said, breaking records

indicators.note: breaking says the letter cuts into the middle of the records

parts.note: annals are yearly historical records
U is how the word you sounds, as in text-speak

explanation.surface: Someone describing things that break records year after year.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearbooks and similar publications come out once a year, as do plants that live a single season.

clue.text: Since 1882, it marks success in tests for trees

definitions.text: Since 1882, it marks success in tests
definitions.meaning: the urn contested by England and Australia in Test cricket dates from 1882
the ash is a common deciduous tree

explanation.surface: Something awarded since 1882 for doing well in forestry tests.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the cricket series between England and Australia; the trophy is a small urn, and 'tests' means Test matches, not exams.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket trophy and the plural of a woodland tree share one spelling.

clue.text: Opening of games at Scottish town that got off to flying start in 1930

definitions.text: that got off to flying start in 1930

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
Wick is a town in Caithness, in the far north of Scotland

explanation.surface: A Highland town that hosted the first event of some games in 1930.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying start' is literal: the London airport opened as an aerodrome in 1930.
explanation.definitionFit: The London airport began as an aerodrome in 1930, so it started with flights.

clue.text: Properties split among people in 1117

parts.note: the first two digits of 1117 point to 11-across, whose solution is a newspaper's name
the last two digits of 1117 point to 17-across, the noted runners

explanation.surface: Holiday homes divided between owners back in the twelfth century.
explanation.walkthrough: 1117 looks like a year but is two clue numbers side by side: 11-across followed by 17-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Holiday flats owned jointly, each buyer getting a slice of the year, are shared properties.

clue.text: Takes off a Romantic author (1795-1821)

indicators.note: off, as in gone off, says the letters of the word before it are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone does an impression of a Romantic poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes off' reads as one phrase meaning mimics; 'off' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: John Keats, who lived from 1795 to 1821, was a leading English Romantic poet.

clue.text: Noted runners from previous era hurrying back

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Famous athletes from a bygone age rushing home.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the hidden step no indicator; 'from' is that signal. SERAH spans previouS ERA Hurrying and 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: These long-eared animals are known for speed, as in the fable of the tortoise and its rival.

clue.text: Like some numbers, within moderation always

indicators.note: within says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Moderation is always the way with some figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers expressible as a fraction of two integers form a class in mathematics.

clue.text: In 2001 he computed a bit less than 45 minutes?

indicators.note: a bit less than says a small piece, the last letter, is removed

parts.note: a football match half lasts 45 minutes

explanation.surface: A question about some calculation from 2001 that came in just under three quarters of an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 2001 is the film 2001: A Space Odyssey, not the year; its computer is HAL 9000.
explanation.definitionFit: HAL 9000 is the talking computer in Kubrick's film 2001: A Space Odyssey.

clue.text: Male, having no heart about middle of 60s, was intimidating

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: about says the word for heartless goes round the next letter

parts.note: fruit with its core removed has been cored

indicators.note: the middle of a seven-letter word is its fourth letter

parts.note: the 60s, spelt out, are the sixties

explanation.surface: A heartless man around the mid-sixties who bullied people.
explanation.definitionFit: To browbeat or bully someone is to hector them, after the Trojan hero.

clue.text: Agreement commemorated in 2015 revised as act (anagram)

indicators.note: something revised has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A historic charter marked in 2015, rewritten as legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: '(anagram)' looks like a note to the solver but is part of the fodder: ACT plus ANAGRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1215 charter between King John and his barons had its 800th anniversary celebrated in 2015.

clue.text: Lecherous racist misbehaving around end of century

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters go round the end letter
misbehaving says the letters of racist act out of order
the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A bigot behaving badly at the close of a century, and lustful too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaving' makes SATRIC from RACIST; 'around' puts it round Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Satyrs of Greek myth were lustful, so behaving like one means being lewd.

clue.text: From 2020, produces scores in sections over short time

indicators.note: over here means covering, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: bits are sections or pieces
sec, short for second, is a brief moment

explanation.surface: From 2020 on, someone gets results in a series of short sections.
explanation.walkthrough: Cutting 2020 in two gives 20 and 20, and a score is twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting 2020 into two equal halves gives twenty and twenty, which are two scores.

clue.text: Like hundreds of dates accepted by male singer, American tough guy

indicators.note: accepted by says the first letters are taken inside the singer

parts.note: a bass is the lowest male voice
most dates we use are AD, Anno Domini

explanation.surface: A deep-voiced singer who goes on lots of dates and is a hard man.
explanation.definitionFit: In US slang a tough, intimidating person is a badass.

clue.text: Preserve commercial area in country since 1867

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it in tins
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: Instructions for tinning food in a business zone of a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Confederation of 1867 created this North American dominion, which marks it as a nation since then.

clue.text: Fun starting in 1913 irritated a lot left out

parts.note: cross means irritated

indicators.note: left out says the letter for left is removed

parts.note: a world of difference means a lot of it

explanation.surface: Some entertainment that began in 1913 annoyed those excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the standard abbreviation for left. Arthur Wynne's word-cross ran in the New York World in 1913.
explanation.definitionFit: The first such grid puzzle appeared in a New York newspaper in December 1913, and it is a pastime.

clue.text: Hint, having book set in 1728, say

indicators.note: set in says the letter is placed inside the word for hint

parts.note: a cue is a prompt or hint

explanation.surface: A clue suggesting a book set in the year 1728.
explanation.walkthrough: 1728 looks like a year but is twelve times twelve times twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: 1728 is 12 multiplied by itself three times, so it is an example of a third power.

clue.text: Small rescue vessel, in 1945, liberated part of the British Isles

definitions.text: in 1945, liberated part of the British Isles

parts.note: Noah's ark saved animals from the flood

explanation.surface: A little lifeboat liberating part of Britain at the end of the war.
explanation.walkthrough: The German occupation of the Channel Islands ended in May 1945.
explanation.definitionFit: This small Channel Island was occupied by Germany until 1945, and it lies within the British Isles.

clue.text: Dispersed in mass burial in 1666

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Bodies scattered in a plague pit during the year of the Great Plague and Fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Dryden's poem 'Annus Mirabilis' named 1666, the year of the Great Fire of London; the plague-pit surface fits that era.
explanation.definitionFit: Dryden used the Latin phrase for 'year of wonders' as the title of his poem about 1666.

clue.text: By the sound of it, a Channel Island providing oversea refuge in 1746

indicators.note: By the sound of it says the word for the channel is heard, not spelt

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite television channel

explanation.surface: A Channel Island that gave someone sanctuary over the water in 1746.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel Island' looks like one phrase (Jersey, Sark); split it into a TV channel and an island. Bonnie Prince Charlie fled 'over the sea to Skye' in 1746.
explanation.definitionFit: After Culloden, Charles Edward Stuart escaped to this Hebridean isle, as the Skye Boat Song recalls.

clue.text: MP in 1983, initially, he was recalled for 1984

definitions.meaning: Tony ... was first elected to Parliament for Sedgefield in 1983
George Orwell, author of the novel 1984, was born Eric ..., so that was his original name

explanation.surface: An MP elected in 1983 who is remembered for 1984.
explanation.definitionFit: The future Labour prime minister entered the Commons in 1983, and Orwell's birth surname was the same.

clue.text: Eve of historic event in 1916, for which date's varying with year

indicators.note: varying says these letters change their order

explanation.surface: The day before a famous uprising, whose date shifts from year to year.
explanation.walkthrough: The Easter Rising in Dublin began on Easter Monday 1916, so the day before was the Sunday; Easter's date moves every year.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dublin Rising started on Easter Monday 1916, so its eve was the Sunday festival.
